rows.subtype: Approach: contingency planning for weather and delays [Thinking]
rows.description: They prepare an indoor option for an outdoor function during monsoon and keep a small reserve for surprises. When rain arrives, the shift takes an hour instead of a crisis.

rows.subtopic: Planning a wedding and family expectations
rows.subtype: Approach: pausing to reset after a conflict over guests [Revision]
rows.description: After a heated fight over the guest list, they step back, agree on a cap and a rule for exceptions, and explain it kindly to both families with the reasons.

rows.subtype: Approach: laying out all income, debts and goals openly [Thinking]
rows.description: Newly married, a couple lists salaries, education loan EMIs, savings and plans. Seeing the whole picture together lets them reason as one team rather than guess about each other.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, resource and budget planning, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: three-account structure of joint and personal money [Action]
rows.description: They open a joint account for rent and bills, each contributing in proportion to income, and keep separate accounts for personal spending. This gives shared security and individual freedom.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, resource and budget planning, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: setting a monthly money meeting [Action]
rows.description: Every first Sunday they review expenses for thirty minutes with tea. Small problems are discussed early, and neither feels ambushed by a big purchase.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, resource and budget planning, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: values-first planning about saving versus spending [Thinking]
rows.description: One partner wants to save for a flat, the other values travel. They agree on a percentage for each goal, so neither feels their priority is dismissed.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, resource and budget planning

rows.subtype: Approach: one partner managing everything without discussion [Pitfall]
rows.description: Assuming it is easier, the husband handles all money matters. His wife does not know the loans or savings, and a sudden expense causes tension and mistrust.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, resource and budget planning, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: hiding a debt or spending to avoid a fight [Pitfall]
rows.description: One partner conceals a credit card balance, hoping to clear it quietly. When it comes out, the concern shifts from the amount to broken trust, which takes longer to repair.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: resource and budget planning, values-first planning

rows.description: Seeing colleagues buy cars and holidays, the couple raises their spending without checking their own budget. Within months they rely on credit cards and argue frequently.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: building an emergency fund first [Action]
rows.description: They decide to hold six months of expenses in a liquid account before big goals. A job loss scare later shows why, as they get through it without borrowing.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, resource and budget planning, values-first planning
